canonicalExplanation.summary: A client-side router maps **URLs to views** without full page reloads. With React Router you declare routes like `<Route path="courses/:courseId" element={<Course />} />`, nest them inside a layout that renders an `<Outlet />`, and navigate with `<Link to="/courses/css">`. Every view keeps a real **address**: it can be bookmarked, shared, refreshed, and reached with Back and Forward. But the router only runs **after** the browser has loaded your app. When someone refreshes `/courses/css`, the **server** must answer that path with `index.html` (a fallback rule), or they'll get a 404.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A learner shares a link to `/courses/css`. Clicking around inside the app works perfectly, but opening the link fresh gives the host's "404 Not Found" page. Navigating to /courses/c renders the course view and refreshing that URL is served by configured hosting. In this lesson you'll implement nested routes and verify direct, link and back-forward navigation.

```predict
{"question": "Inside the app, a Link to /courses/css works. A fresh visit to the same URL returns 404. Where's the problem?", "options": ["In the React routes", "In the hosting: the server has no file at that path and needs a fallback to index.html"], "answer": 1, "why": "The browser asks the server first. Only index.html loads the router."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know the **Remote data and asynchronous UI** module, **URL and history state** (paths, search and history), and **Children and composition**, since layouts wrap child routes.

examples.title: A course URL that survives refresh
examples.situation: Navigating to /courses/c renders the course view and refreshing that URL is served by configured hosting.
walkthrough: **Declare routes:** `courses/:courseId` renders Course inside Layout's Outlet.
**Configure hosting:** a rewrite sends /courses/c and other app paths to index.html.
**Check three ways:** click a Link, press Back and Forward, then refresh the URL; each will render the course view.
examples.result: Shared and refreshed course links open the right page instead of a 404.

examples.title: The link that wiped the progress
examples.situation: The navigation uses `<a href>` tags. Moving between lessons resets the quiz progress kept in React state.
walkthrough: Plain anchors trigger a full page load.
The whole React app restarts and its state is lost.
Fix: use `<Link to=...>` so the router changes views without reloading.
examples.result: Moving between lessons keeps the quiz progress.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: A client router makes every deep URL work on the server automatically.
misconceptions.correction: The router runs in the browser after index.html loads. A direct request for a deep path goes to the server first, which needs a fallback rule to return index.html.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "A course URL that survives refresh", what did the host need?

analogy.example: A client router is like **the receptionist inside a building** directing you to rooms. It works once you're inside. If someone gives the taxi driver a room number (a deep URL), the **building's front gate** (the server) must know to let them in through reception (index.html).
usefulFor: remembering router inside, server at the gate
Link = walking between rooms without leaving
limitations: Receptionists don't need rewrites; servers do.
An `a href` is leaving and re-entering the building.

trace.textAlternative: Checking three kinds of navigation. Step 1, Link: reload is no; view is Course c. Navigating to /courses/c renders the course view without a reload. Step 2, Refresh: server returns is index.html; view is Course c. Refreshing that URL is served by configured hosting. Step 3, Back: URL is /courses; view is CourseList.
